burru.title: A Popular Djembe Rhythm, "Burru" with Joakim Lartey @ Tribal Rhyhtm Gathering 2018
burru.description:
Tribal Rhythms Gathering happens in Upstate New York every summer. Full details at: http://www.didgeproject.com/gathering

Joakim Lartey is a drummer/percussionist, storyteller, educator and sound designer. He was co-founder, lead singer and percussionist of Woodstock’s Futu Futu. He is engaged in a lifelong exploration of recording technology and the fusion of traditional/ancient and contemporary musical forms. He has collaborated/played with Natalie Merchant, Jack DeJohnette, John Hall, Baba Olatunji among others…

He currently performs with the duo Joakim & Chris [with guitarist Chris Lane] and The Sonark Trio [with multi instrumentalist Thomas Workman and cellist Gabriel Dresdale]

*******************

Didge Project features music tutorials and instrument reviews. Follow us:

http://www.didgeproject.com
http://www.facebook.com/didgeproject
https://www.youtube.com/didgeproject7

burru.setting: Tribal Rhythm Gathering 2018, Upstate New York; uploaded February 1, 2019.
burru.caption: Joakim Lartey teaches an Afro-Jamaican Burru pattern on djembe at the 2018 Tribal Rhythm Gathering in Upstate New York. Didge Project published the lesson in 2019.
listening_prompts: Follow the recurring sequence Lartey demonstrates: two bass strokes, two tone strokes, two bass strokes and four tone strokes. The producer labels bass B and tone T.
Keep your attention on the return of the low bass sound after the brighter tones; this is a teaching pattern with variations, not a claim that every Jamaican Burru performance uses one fixed formula.
Compare the lesson’s isolated drum vocabulary with the second duo demonstration; treat the two as educational performances rather than Christmas procession recordings.
burru.identity_limits: Explicitly named Burru by producer; djembe classroom demonstration in the United States. Not an archival Old Harbour Bay/Spring Village procession.
